rationale:
INCOMING_SWIFT JOB 2. Pins the two ontology types this lane did not emit. `imports` is the family's first-class MODULE-DEPENDENCY label (go #799: with the edge labelled `references`, every module name landed in the references target surface and a module is not a symbol — measured over 800 corpus files, 671/671 references edges had a module name as target). `exports` is Swift's export surface, which has no keyword: it is the declared `visibility_modifier` token, plus `@_exported import` (the one construct whose name is an export). `references` is KEPT alongside `imports` on purpose — the shared differential's swift oracle derives `references` from import_declaration, so dropping it here would manufacture MISSING rows this lane cannot fix; bash publishes the same pair (isSourceImport + isSourceDependency), and the two metadata markers keep the claims distinct. Source is `root`, never a module name: a Swift module is a build TARGET, not a file, so naming it after the file's leaf would assert a module that does not exist. The fixture also pins the ownership defect the lane's independent span oracle found: `contains` whose SOURCE is a function is forbidden (143 such edges on the 800-file corpus draw).

SUPERSESSION 2026-10-25 (rows only; the analyzer's emission was already right). The original expectation table pinned TWO things the lane's own ruling contradicts, and both were measured against a PASSING sibling fixture rather than argued: (1) MEMBER exports — `count`, `constructor`, `bump`, `added` were pinned as `exports`, while the rationale above states DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT4 narrowed the label to FILE-SCOPE declarations and `scoped-import-metadata`/`exports-visibility` forbid member rows; those four are now `contains` (pinned here) and forbidden as exports. (2) The KIND-RESTRICTED import `import struct Swift.Optional` pinned the dotted path as an `imports` TARGET, while `scoped-import-metadata` pins the module (`Single`) as the target and the spelled path as a `references` row under R10; the corrected rows are `imports -> Swift` (with isScopedImport/moduleSpecifier/scopedKind/scopedItem) and `references -> Swift.Optional`. (3) The `exports` metadata vocabulary is DERIV's: `exportForm`/`accessLevel`/`reExport`, not the pre-DERIV `visibility`/`isModuleSurface`/`isReExport`. The old table is kept beside this file as imports-exports.expectation.superseded-2026-10-25.json so the change is auditable.
